messages:
incident_bot: Paging: oncall-sre. Elevated 5xx/timeouts observed across gateway in eu-west-1 for generation routes. Error spike started ~2m ago. Alert: gateway 504 rate up 18% over baseline.

alex_wu: seeing same from dashboard — per-route latency spike and batcher-queue depth climbing. Looks like scheduler backlog on cluster gpu-pool-eu-2.

maya_khan: confirming: batching queue depth = 870 (baseline ~50). Head-of-line wait times showing long tail > 12s. Many small requests stuck behind large prompt jobs.

henry: logs show repeated kv-cache growth on a subset of shards, causing GC/backpressure. Also seeing gateway: upstream timeout while waiting for batcher response.

alex_wu: quick mitigation ideas: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 8 on problematic model to force more but smaller batches; 2) enable emergency route to cpu-fallback pool for short prompts; 3) temporarily route 30% of traffic to us-east warm pool. Which is fastest?

sasha: oncall-sre, are you able to flip batch size flag? I can cut the routing after.

oncall-sre: ack, coming in. I'll take lead. Paging to oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: taking pager. Running sanity checks on cluster nodes. Starting with cutting max_batch_size for model:open-ggml-1 to 8 on gpu-pool-eu-2 via orch flag.

oncall-sre: command I ran: `redwoodctl set-config --pool gpu-pool-eu-2 --model open-ggml-1 --max-batch-size 8 --reason "live mitigation - hol blocking"`

oncall-sre: patch applied across 4 nodes, rolling restart of serving proxies in progress.

maya_khan: after the change, queue depth dropped from 870 -> 340 in ~40s. 5xx rate trending down but still above baseline. Head latencies improved for small requests.

henry: started emergency route: `route-manager add-fallback --from generation --to warm-us-east --pct 30 --ttl 20m` — traffic redirect in place.

alex_wu: also toggled prefix KV caching eviction threshold to free ~5GB on affected shards: `runtimectl evict-kv --pool gpu-pool-eu-2 --target 5GB`

sasha: customers impacted? Any premium routes?

oncall-sre: initial sfx shows ~12 requests/min failing for enterprise tenants on eu-west-1 between t0 and now. We've opened CSM channel.

csm_bryan: I have the customer list for the affected shard. Messaging support to prioritize customers with SLA. Drafting templated status message for impacted customers (will post once we confirm stabilization).

alex_wu: metric summary now: gateway 504 rate down from +18% -> +6% in last 2m. Batcher queue depth continuing to fall, currently 120. Average tail latency down from 16s -> 6s. Still monitoring for regressions.

oncall-sre: rolling restart completed. No node OOMs during restart. CPU and GPU util normalized.

henry: root cause hypothesis: a set of long prompts (internal evals) created very large batches, KV growth, and head-of-line blocking combined with aggressive batch size autoscaling. When the KV working set expanded it slowed token emission, propagating timeouts at the gateway.

maya_khan: follow-ups: 1) disable aggressive autoscale policy on gpu-pool-eu-2 for 30m; 2) add a prefilter on generation route to throttle very long prompts or route them to a dedicated long-job queue; 3) add alert for kv-cache-growth > 3GB/5m per shard.

oncall-sre: implemented short-term change: set autoscale.cooldown=120s for pool. Will revert after postmortem.

alex_wu: documenting mitigation steps in incident doc. Can someone take handoff for post-incident follow-up and customer comms?

csm_bryan: I'll own customer comms and gather impact window + affected tenants list.

sasha: I'll own the runbook updates: add prefilter rule + autoscale safe defaults + a suggested emergency routing playbook.

maya_khan: I'll file an infra ticket to investigate kv-cache GC heuristics and model-specific batch sizing heuristics.

oncall-sre: last check: 5xx rate at +1.2% over baseline, queue depth stable at 40, tail latency median ~180ms. Moving to monitoring-only.

alex_wu: thanks all. We'll keep thread open for 30m before archiving. Add any late regressions here. :thumbsup:

incident_bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Links: https://observability.redwood/incident/2471353099 (perf graphs), https://alerts.redwood/2471353099

maya_khan: note for postmortem: seeds to reproduce were two concurrent large-batch eval jobs from internal bench that started at almost same time. Add isolation for eval workloads vs prod traffic.

henry: FYI I preserved heap dumps and KV snapshots for 3 affected shards to the artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/2471353099/

csm_bryan: posting customer note now.

alex_wu: closing handoff. If anything flares up ping this thread and we'll re-escalate.
